q: Is site-mixed concrete higher or lower carbon than ready-mix concrete?
title: Site-mixed vs ready-mix concrete carbon
short: Start with the cement per cubic metre in each mix, times the supplier's factor. Then add mixing energy: site mixer diesel at 2.68 kg CO2 per litre, and for ready mix the plant electricity and truck mixer diesel.
audience: Building contractors and developers choosing how to source concrete

ul: Cement content per cubic metre, from the mix design or batch sheets.
Use of fly ash or slag in place of some cement.
Mixing energy at site or plant.

p: Ready mix suppliers can give batch tickets with cement and blend per load. For site mixing, divide cement bags used by cubic metres poured over the same period.
A site mixer the contractor runs is Scope 1. Bought ready mix, including its plant and delivery, is Scope 3 purchased goods.

example.title: Worked example: per cubic metre (illustrative inputs)
lines: Site mixer: 0.5 litre diesel per m3 x 2.68 = 1.34 kg CO2 per m3
Ready mix: plant 2 kWh x 0.710 = 1.42 kg, plus truck mixer 1 litre x 2.68 = 2.68 kg, so 4.10 kg CO2 per m3
Mixing difference: 4.10 minus 1.34 = 2.76 kg CO2 per m3
Cement: site mix 340 kg vs ready mix design 320 kg per m3, a 20 kg difference
Cement difference: 20 kg x the cement factor per kg from the supplier
example.note: Values are illustrative; use batch tickets, cement issue records and the cement supplier's factor.

senseible: Senseible reads diesel invoices, fuel slips and site electricity bills into a dated, fingerprinted record per project, so a contractor can hand a client Scope 1 and 2 figures with the document behind each line. Estimates from hours or distance are labelled as estimates.
